purpose: Historical legally documented monetary outcomes, not a measure of toxic harm, fault, mortality or an additive company score.

USD.method: US CPI-U all items, U.S. city average, annual mean (NSA); reference 2025. 2025 BLS annual average omits October due to the federal funding lapse.

BRL.method: IBGE IPCA calendar-year Dec/Dec rates compounded after nominal base year through December 2025. The 2021 agreement was signed in February; December-2021 convention is only a standardized comparator, not a contractual indexation calculation.

cases.notes: Payment to the state is not a quantification of individual illness or total ecological loss.

cases.hazard: Mine-tailings dam failure / watershed and communities
cases.disposition: Judicial agreement; separate individual and criminal proceedings remain distinct

obligation.kind: Total agreed collective reparation package; includes works performed, future work and transfers

payment.detail: Minas Gerais environmental authority reported R$18.2bn already paid toward different agreement obligations after one year; covers multiple payment/implementation periods. This is a dated historical lower bound, not a current 2026 total. Separately, Vale's June 2026 investor reporting discloses US$15.172bn of total cumulative Brumadinho-related outlays since 2019 across a broader scope, including dam decommissioning, individual/emergency compensation and other work. That broader figure is not the cash paid under this exact 2021 agreement and must not be substituted for, added to, or currency-converted into this R$18.2bn historical observation.

cases.notes: Agreement contains both duties to perform works and duties to transfer funds. Paid figure and package overlap; they must never be added. Multi-year cash has no single valid inflation base year.

cases.matter: Exxon Valdez natural-resource restoration civil settlement
cases.disposition: 1991 court-approved civil settlement; historic Exxon Corporation predecessor, not a present-day ExxonMobil operating record

obligation.kind: 1991 settlement promise across ten-year installments, distinct from criminal fine and restitution

cases.hazard: 1984 methyl isocyanate release / fatal and nonfatal exposure
cases.disposition: 1989 Supreme Court of India settlement order, distinct from any scientific accounting of the disaster

obligation.kind: Combined U.S.-dollar equivalent settlement for victims; $425m allocated to UCC and $45m to Indian affiliate (the latter paid in rupees)

payment.detail: India's Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals says $470m in compensation was deposited in February 1989. The Supreme Court's payment mechanics split the settlement between Union Carbide Corporation ($425m, including a $5m U.S. interim payment from 1985) and Union Carbide India Ltd. (rupee equivalent of $45m). Do not attribute $470m to each company, assume all cash was transferred in 1989, or treat the USD total as a single-currency bank transfer.

allocations.basis: Court-stated USD contribution; includes earlier $5m interim payment
Court-stated USD equivalent; actually paid in Indian rupees

cases.notes: The $470m is a collective legal settlement, not a valuation of the lives lost, lifetime medical injuries, continuing contamination, or remediation needs. The official victim-disbursement program extended long after the companies' settlement deposit. Later corporate changes must not be confused with which historical entities made the 1989 settlement.

payment.detail: U.S. DOJ and EPA both expressly record that the defendants paid $5.15bn PLUS interest to the Anadarko Litigation Trust on January 23, 2015.
